# The Black Mountain Boyz

*Pages PDF 42-51*

## ## the Black Mountain Boyz
## **Extortion and Ambition**
Harboth Skullrenda is an Orc with big ideas and a strong desire for a comeback. He wants his own Waaagh! and he’s got a plan to get there. Years of leading his tribe have given him the experience he needs to use both horrendous violence and basic cunning to take what he wants. Harboth just needs to watch his back — not all the bosses are convinced he’s still got what it takes. 

Harboth set a few lads to follow him and, incredibly, the trader returned with the goods. Harboth saw the potential in this arrangement and, after a few months, the tribe set up a toll, which was really more of an extortion operation. When Harboth could restrain his lads for long enough, they’d let the odd traveller through, who spread the word north and south of the pass that the Orcs in the Black Mountain could be bargained with… usually. 

Years ago, Harboth founded a camp in Black Fire Pass south of Zan Mingol and for a few years, the tribe thrived. At first, they killed any Human or Dwarf merchant convoys that passed their way. 

The arrangement worked well, but Harboth hadn’t thought very far ahead. Eventually, an army from Karak Hirn marched to the pass and chased the Black Mountain Boyz away from their camp. 

As the tribe grew, they eventually waylaid all the travellers who passed through a narrow defile near their main base — and the main route through the Black Mountains became impassable. An Empire trader desperate to reach the Border Princes offered to bring more weapons if Harboth’s boyz let him travel to Munzig. 

Now Harboth and his tribe wander the Black Mountains, extracting loot with menaces and following the usual Orc pursuits — killing, maiming, and making a lot of noise. The tribe has diminished in strength due to their wars and wandering, and Harboth needs to work hard to cling to power. 

## **Disposition of the Warband**
The Black Mountain Boyz are a smaller tribe than it was during the glory days of the Black Fire camp, and Harboth knows that it’s going to take some serious conquests to grow it again. Below Harboth, each boss has his own mob of Orcs who form a boisterous band of compatriots. 

The inner circle of the tribe consists of: 

- Harboth Skullrenda is surrounded by 12 Big ‘Uns (Orc Elites), a retinue of the hardest Orcs in the tribe. Pigbok carries Harboth’s banner. 

- Yaskin is an especially violent Orc who dresses in the best plunder. 

- Old Balnag, is the oldest Orc in the tribe and full of stories of great Waaagh!s of the past. 

- Daggot is an unusually quiet Orc. The other bosses assume he’s smart, but he’s actually too stupid to know what’s going on most of the time. 

- Ugdrakk is untrustworthy, because he prefers a bow to his Dwarf Tickler. 

There are 95 Boyz (Orc Soldiers) — nasty bruisers who stay in line as long as a fight comes along fairly regularly and Harboth doesn’t go too soft on the tribe’s victims. They carry nasty hooked cleavers which Harboth has dubbed ‘Dwarf Ticklers’. The Black Mountain Boyz enjoy drinking stolen Dwarf booze and the odd punchup. The whole system of exchange involved in Harboth’s crude form of trade is far too complicated for most of them to understand, but the Orc chief ’s fists are pretty easy to comprehend — so they won’t always kill travellers on sight. 

- Balnag’s Rockstabbas — so-called because they once mistook a field of boulders for Dwarf Rangers. 

- Stunty’s Nightmare — Yaskin’s rowdy mob who always seem to grab the best loot. 

- Green Thumpas — Daggot’s mob. 

- Rusty Slicers — remnants of the former Greytoof tribe, now subsumed into the Black Mountain Boyz. 

The other half of the tribe are 84 Arrer Boyz (Orc Skirmishers). These Orcs are a little skinnier than the other Boyz and there’s a rivalry between the two camps — the Arrer Boyz think the Boyz are thick and the Boyz think the Arrer Boyz are a ‘bit runty’. They’re both right. 

- Da Red Arrers — Ugdrakk tends to band with this mob. 

- Dedeye Lads. 

- Skarface Killaz. 

A ragtag crew of 20–40 menials do the worst jobs for the Black Mountain Boyz. Runty Orcs and skulking Gobbos to cook, fetch, carry, and act as punch bags for the Boyz. 

## **Uniform**
Black Mountain Boyz wear ragged tunics and breeches stolen from travellers, patched and filthy. Some strut about in rusty chainmail and leather armour, a sure sign of status in the tribe. 

## **Shield Design**
Shields depict the most noteworthy victims in a moment of agony. These are painted by Muckvey, a Goblin slave with unusual artistic skill. 

## **Battlecry**
“Krump da stunties!” 

## Bring Back Notlob!
When Harboth’s tribe occupied Black Fire Pass, they were joined by the inventive Notlob. This Orc has ‘invented’ (copied from Goblins) the bolt thrower. Due to Harboth’s failure to appreciate Notlob’s genius, the Orc artillerist left the tribe in a huff. This still rankles with Harboth. He’s desperate enough to have Humies take on the job of bringing Notlob back. 

## Unfinished Business
The Black Mountain Boyz were badly beaten at the Battle of Bauer’s Farm by Baron Olaf von Grünfeld’s Own Regiment of Foot. Ever since then, the Big ‘Uns have been rumbling that Harboth may have lost it. He wants to prove a point and go back to sort out Baron Olaf’s regiment. 

## Olde Weirde’s Incunabulum
Though it is well known the wilderness of the Empire is home to many tribes of Goblins, it seems to be free of Orcs. Is this true? To examine the issue, we must be clear on our taxonomy. Is a Goblin a small Orc, or an Orc a large Goblin? Is one a subset of the other? Are they the same thing, essentially, of a different size or are they as separate as, for example, a Human and a Halfling? Though Professors von Gronighof and Pfaff and myself have had many a debate on the subject, I remain undecided. For the purposes of this article, I assume they are different but collectively can be called Greenskins. 

Some posit that Orcs are so belligerent and uncontrollable that they cannot survive in the Empire at all. They will immediately attack all settlements they can, drawing inevitable retaliation by the local lords, or indeed the provincial army, leading to their destruction. While Goblins, it is clear, can lie low, survive unobtrusively in the margins, attack opportunistically, but avoid being so serious a threat that the generals of Imperial armies are moved to destroy them. Perhaps Goblins are able to hunt and gather, and even perform rudimentary cultivation, whereas Orcs are not prepared to labour in this way. 

Therefore, Orcs are the architects of their own inevitable destruction. I should say that this destruction is only inevitable due to the excellent Imperial armies, the bravery of her people, and the protection of Sigmar. But it is still inevitable. 

Orcs outside the Empire survive by raiding and conquering. And sometimes, through fortunate circumstances, they thrive, and when they thrive, they are brought into conflict with their fellows. This leads to the rise and fall of several warlords. When things go well, they fight each other and then through mutual destruction and the attrition of war, their numbers recede once more. And the cycle begins again. This phenomenon can be seen with foxes in a rabbit field or stirpike in a fishpond. That is not to say we are merely rabbits and the Orcs are stirpike. 

But occasionally this natural balance is thrown out of kilter by the rise of a singular warlord. In their shadow, the lesser warlords either perish or become subservient. 

And the various tribes and factions are able to unite for a single purpose. This is known as Waaagh!, a barely controllable uprising of multitudes of Greenskins united temporarily for the purpose of death and destruction. 

When a Waaagh! is directed at the Empire, then she cannot resist it without severe damage and suffering. It cannot be predicted, and it would be unreasonable to expect the Imperial armies to react to and defeat a Waaagh! in its early stages. Like a wave crashing against the shore, it is inevitable that the Waaagh! does the greater part of its destruction before it can be seriously opposed. Therefore, the people of the Empire must live with the constant possibility of sudden assault. 

Fortunately, it is inevitable that the forces that brought the Waaagh! together must end, as disunity and division occur throughout the Greenskin army. The urge for squabbling and animosity among their kind can only be overcome for short periods, and this is usually to the gain of the individual tribes. Once they have sufficient plunder, they are apt to return to their homelands. Jealousy and rivalry among the commanders are likely to lead to in-fighting, and no Waaagh! is known to have persisted after the death of the leader who inspired it. 

Such an analysis may seem cold, but the inevitability of the attack, and the inevitability of its ultimate failure makes it feel like an Orc Waaagh! should no more disturb us than a violent storm or earthquake. Do not take this holistic and strategic view to indicate that the death and destruction caused by the Waaagh! is anything but a tragedy, and its ending not to the credit of the Imperial armies. In the process of a wave crashing upon the beach, every grain of sand has its story. 

I have heard it said that Orcs are so belligerent that they can never be bargained with, but this is not the case. I have encountered a band which was amenable to negotiation. We were travelling through Black Fire Pass and heard that a huge Greenskin Waaagh! was coming our way. This turned out to be untrue, but a sizeable force was blocking the route. They did not stream down from the mountains carrying all before them, they simply sat up in the pass waiting for travellers to come to them. 

We approached the blockade tentatively, thinking this to be a trap, but the Orcs had set up some sort of toll system. This was arguably similar to the ones that can be found on roads all across the Empire, but without going to the trouble of constructing the road in the first place. The Orcs there called themselves the Black Mountain Boyz and seemed to think they had the authority to charge us for using the pass. 

Their first demand from us was weapons, but we were not able to fulfil that request. Kaia’s short sword is remarkably fine and I suspect has a unique provenance but the Orcs did not rate it as anything more than a toothpick and Sovrissniz refused to put up any of her weapons for negotiation. Then they talked about beer. I know Professor von Gronighof has a cache of Bretonnian brandy he tries to keep to himself, but we both agreed that would be wasted on the Orc palate. 

In the end, we settled on two pouches of silver and our packed lunches. The landlady of the inn where we had spent the previous night had been good enough to make up some meals for the day’s travel. We handed these over and, surprisingly to my mind, the brutish Greenskins let us pass. It was a small price to pay and I think it showed the Orcs to have surprising versatility in their negotiations. We did not have much they would find useful, but they were able to get something out of us, showing an appreciation for crude economic considerations. 

Had they charged too much of the travellers, or been heavyhanded, then they would have been driven away by the Imperial army in quick time. Much like an Altdorf haberdasher or an Eilhart wine merchant must, they pitched a price point that the market would tolerate. Of course, they were moved on by an Imperial army eventually, but this was more of a political choice by Averland forces, rather than market forces. 

We travelled down the pass. After several hours, we spotted another band of Orcs. These were not sedentary, however. They were striding down the valley towards us. We could see that they meant harm, and quickly decided to retreat. Sovrissniz spotted a defendable crag she said would be suitable for a glorious last stand. But when the rest of us ignored her, and returned the way we came as quickly as we could, she joined us (though she spent next two days in high dudgeon). 

It is clear to me that inter-tribe rivalry among Greenskins is one of the most emphatic drivers of their behaviour. Their natural belligerence coupled with their antipathy for rivals meant that conflict between the two factions was inevitable. 

Besides, the Black Mountain Boyz had a decent racket going on here. They did not want to upset that. They could not have another tribe raiding the nearby settlements and provoking an Imperial response. The Black Mountain Boyz were simply protecting their position as market leaders. 

They tell me that in some of the poorer areas of Altdorf, shopkeepers and artisans are often forced to pay local hoodlums to protect their businesses from other gangs. This is not a choice they are given, and the protection is effectively from the very gang that extorts the money in the first place. The Orcs were behaving just like this. It could certainly be a cause for reflection that the rulers of a barony on the far-flung edge of the Empire might act so emphatically to end such a racket but similar activity going on mere yards from the Imperial palace is tolerated. 

In any case, the Black Mountain Boyz let us return to the shelter of their settlement, and then mustered a force to go out and punish the Greenskin raiders. After a couple of hours, the battle was done and the survivors of the invading Orc band were fleeing back into the mountains. We were safe to go on our way once more. And besides, while the Orcs were fighting, Kaia used the distraction to sneak into their supply tent and repossess our purloined purses and packed lunches. 

. 

The Orcs were determined and persistent. We ended up retreating all the way back to the Black Mountain Boyz’ camp. We were now caught between two belligerent forces with no way out. Or so we thought. But Professor von Gronighof went to the camp and insisted on the protection of the Black Mountain Boyz. After all, we were toll-paying customers, and the rival Orcs were invaders. 

The Black Mountain Orcs decided that von Gronighof had a reasonable point and promised him the invaders would be dealt with. Despite what he called his ‘masterstroke of double-play,’ my feeling is that he did not sway the Black Mountain Boyz one way or the other. 

## **Tactics**
Small groups of Orcs (a Big ‘Un or Champion with 5–10 Boyz) wander close to camp to look for victims to loot and or kill. They’re not bright enough to ambush — they just rush the target when they see it. 

Arrer Boyz prefer to sneak up in groups of 8–10 to take shots at adversaries. They stay in cover shooting for about 1d10 rounds before deciding to charge in. 

In large numbers, the Black Mountain Boyz form into mobs in a straggling line — usually three mobs of Boyz and three of Arrer Boyz. Harboth bellows orders while the Boyz taunt the enemy and then charge, while the Arrer Boyz fire over their heads to disrupt the enemy’s line. 

Harboth’s most cunning tactic is “da deal”. When he thinks adversaries can offer something he wants, he negotiates and holds back the tribe. This is an extortion racket rather than an honest trade. Even if the deal looks sound, some bosses may attack anyway — especially Balnag or Yaskin. 

## **At Ease**
Wherever Harboth’s tribe pitch up, they drag rocks and logs into a barrier to block passage, then fashion rough shelters while the menials dig a huge pit just outside the camp where they perform their ablutions and throw victims (alive or dead). There are several Big ‘Uns and at least 10 Boyz on guard keeping the fires going at all times, while the rest of the tribe laze around. 

The Arrer Boyz go hunting for food — the decent grub they bring to Harboth keeps them protected against the scorn of the Boyz who think they’re not Orcy enough. The tribe clears an area of rocks where they can scrap for entertainment. Most fights happen are weaponless brawls, but if tempers boil over, or Harboth wants a proper laugh, fights are to the death. 

## **Empty Yer Pockets Easy Encounter**
Harboth ordered some lads to barricade a nearby road or narrow gorge and ‘get good stuff ’ off anyone who passes by. So Pigbok dragged a small mob to a promising place to block the path and look mean at anyone who approaches. 

This encounter could happen on any road the Characters are travelling, providing there’s no easy way around the Orcs — they may be hard of thinking, but they’re not completely stupid. Pigbok promised the Boyz either a good scrap or some decent loot, so they’re full of enthusiasm for now. 

The blockade consists of a broken wagon, some logs, and a stinking pile of rags, which covers a Goblin corpse. When the Characters approach, the Orcs yell at them and Pigbok waves his Dwarf Tickler. He has a few words of Reikspiel (or Tilean) which he uses to hail the Party and demand tribute. They can pass if they give him armour, weapons, large amounts of food, or similar. There’s no interest in gold or money. 

The Characters can negotiate, but all Fellowship Tests are **Difficult (–10)** . It’s not easy to convince Pigbok that something is valuable unless it’s obvious — Orcs can only see the worth of something if it’s big or obviously impressive. If negotiation fails, the Orcs fight. 

If the Characters successfully trade something for passage, Pigbok needs to pass an **Average (+20) Leadership** Test to stop the Boyz following the party and attacking them anyway. This encounter is an opportunity to present Orcs as capable of more than just violence. While Pigbok’s party are thuggish and threatening, it’s possible to get past them without a fight. 

Pigbok’s band consists of: 

- Pigbok (Orc Elite) standing on a rock and shouting. 

- Four Boyz (Orc Soldiers) waiting behind the barricade, ready to charge. 

- One Arrer Boy (Skirmisher) with an arrow nocked, in cover behind the wagon. 

## **Krumpin’ by Proxy Medium Encounter**
The Black Mountain Boyz are not a harmonious tribe. Half the Orcs think they can fight better with new methods, while the other half distrust anything which doesn’t feel Orcy enough to their limited imagination. Ugdrakk often takes Da Red Arrers out of camp to practice archery and patrol the area looking for potential threats. It’s also a good chance for him to seethe about insults from other bosses and the Boyz who don’t respect him enough. 

The mob are crashing about in the woods or hills near the Black Mountain Boyz’ current camp, looking for targets to practice shooting. They’re loosing arrows at rocks, trees, and any living creature which comes within range. If the Characters are in the vicinity, they’ll likely hear the unsubtle sound of Orcs prowling around. Soon after, the Arrer Boyz start shooting at them. 

This could be a combat situation, but Ugdrakk is brooding on Old Balnag, who’s been throwing his weight around by beating up Red Arrers. When Ugdrakk saw the Characters, he formed a plan to get even with Balnag. After softening up the party, Ugdrakk calls a truce and cuffs the Arrer Boyz about the head to stop them shooting. He hails the Characters in broken Reikspiel and tells them he’s going to do them a favour, because he likes the colour of their hats or some equally implausible lie. If the Party listens, he lets them know where Balnag is camped with his Rockstabbas. He explains that the old Orc is a Big Boss planning to invade all the Humie lands. If the Characters promise to deal with the rival boss, he’ll let them go. 

The group with Ugdrakk consists of: 

- Ugdrakk, an Orc Chief who also has _Ranged (Bow)_ +8 (50) and a bow with arrows in his trappings. 

- 14 Arrer Boyz (Orc Skirmishers) who shoot at whatever takes their fancy, with no concentration of fire. 

## **There Goes the Neighbourhood Hard Encounter**
For the last few weeks, traders have stopped visiting the mountain settlement of Staffelhügel and travellers from the mountains no longer come to the town. Gerd, the village headman, has no doubt something is wrong in the Vale of Staffel. When a battered merchant appears at the village gates with tales of Orcs demanding tithes in exchange for ‘safe’ passage, the villager’s fears are confirmed. More than trade is at risk — without grain from the lowlands, some highland villages will starve. 

The Black Mountain Boyz have set up camp right in the middle in the Vale of Staffel. Harboth is well-pleased the tribe is back in the extortion game. Even better, the stretch of valley where they are established is especially defensible with steep sides and rock formations forming natural fortifications. 

Should they investigate, the party meet a swaggering Harboth who mocks them, then demands tribute for passage and to stop his boyz from attacking Staffelhügel and its mine. Yaskin and various other bosses stand behind him, beating their weapons on their shields. The Black Mountain Boyz want armour, cattle and swine, ‘stunty axes’, and a crown for Harboth. 

Dealing with the Black Mountain Boyz is difficult and the longer they take, the more wandering greenskins are drawn to Harboth’s camp. 

If the Characters negotiate successfully and Harboth makes any concessions, there is discord in the camp. Yaskin and several Big ‘Uns argue with Harboth and gesticulate at the party. A fight breaks out — half the Orcs go for the party and attack the rest of the tribe. The other half (mostly Arrer Boyz) attack Yaskin’s side and, opportunistically, take potshots at the party. 

You can move this encounter to anywhere in the southern Empire, northern Tilea or the Border Princes. The force in the camp consists of the whole tribe, as outlined on page 43. 

- Three scared Basic Common Goblins, expected to retrieve and carry any game. 

## **Harboth Skullrenda – Orc Warlord**
Harboth is the Big Boss, a bullying Orc who thinks he deserves more than the diminished tribe currently under his command. He towers over most of his boyz and strides around in a horned helm, fancy red breeches, and a mail coat in reasonably good condition. Harboth loves fighting, but he believes sometimes you can be cunning too. By extorting stuff from travellers, he hopes to build up the Black Mountain Boyz again. 

Unfortunately, Gork and Mork have not favoured him in recent years. He lost his Black Fire Pass camp, some of the lads are giving him funny looks, and various underlings have drifted off to better prospects and bigger fights. Harboth secretly worries he’ll be reduced to stealing cattle in the Border Princes if his luck doesn’t change. 

.

## **Yaskin Forit – Orc Chief**
Yaskin is Harboth’s most important champion, a tough boss with an especially cruel and impatient demeanour. He has a crooked mouth and wears a necklace of Dwarf ears. He wields a particularly nasty-looking Dwarf Tickler, larger than any other Orc in the tribe. Yaskin never removes the helmet he looted from a Dwarf Thane. Although it is now battered, the impressive crest still marks him out amongst his fellow bosses. 

Yaskin is rambunctious and greedy. He doesn’t really like the idea of dealing with non-Orcs without violence, although he is a proud hypocrite — enjoying the spoils of trade more than most of the Black Mountain Boyz. Philosophical consistency doesn’t bother Yaskin at all.

## **Hagblad – Orc Soldier**
Hagblad is a typical Black Mountain Boy — he likes fighting, he likes shouting, and he doesn’t like thinking too much. Hagblad should be content. He gets enough grub and there are plenty of opportunities to hit someone or something hard enough to break bones. 

Yet Hagblad is fed up, and it shows in his disgruntled expression. He thinks he deserves a bigger share of the loot. Fighting as one of Old Balnag’s Rockstabbas, he can’t help feeling the other lads have better gear than him… bigger weapons and so on. Hagblad doesn’t even have any proper armour, just a tatty leather jerkin. 

Hagblad knows Harboth could batter him, but wonders why the Big Boss keeps trying to be cunning rather than brutal. Most of the time, Hagblad goes along with what Old Balnag says, because thinking makes your head hurt and Balnag is quick to knock you about if you don’t do as you’re told.

## **Holg Stuntysticker – Orc Skirmisher**
Holg is an arrer boy who hangs out with the Dedeye Boyz. He reckons he’s the best shot in the mob, which isn’t true. Most Orcs think they’re the best at something.

Holg is pleased with his chainmail vest and helmet, the prize for shooting a stunty off a wall from 50 paces. He doesn’t care that the other lads are jealous, although he sleeps on his stuff in case anyone wants to nick it. 

**Talents:** Accurate Shot, Flee! 

Physically, Holg is a little bit runty — this makes him defensive, even amongst the Arrer Boyz. It’s hard enough the regular Boyz thinking arrers aren’t Orcy enough. Given the right opportunity, he might ‘accidentally’ put an arrow in one of the Big ‘Uns’ backs. 

**Trappings:** Bow and 12 Arrows, Choppa, Helmet, Mail Shirt, Shield 

Unlike Hagblad, Holg thinks Harboth is dragging Orc warfare into the future. As an archer, he likes the idea of inflicting pain at a distance and, based on the faces of the Black Mountain Boyz’ ‘trading partners’, they don’t seem to get much pleasure from paying a toll either.
